absent: Bootconfig tree structure, parsing grammar, verification rules, and error position assignment beyond init and exit.
Btree concurrency rules, mempool sizing and failure behavior, and slab lifetime beyond create and destroy.
Bucket to lock mapping policy and constraints needed for mask based indexing.
Bug trap handling, reporting, and lifetime rules for file and format strings.
Comparator obligations and ordering contract for sorted search beyond delegation.

findings.text: Bootconfig initialization copies caller supplied bytes into owned storage with termination, reserves fixed capacity node storage, then builds and validates the tree. It returns the node count on success, initializes optional position output to failure sentinel, reports diagnostics through optional outputs, and refuses reentry, empty input, oversize input and allocation failures with distinct negative errors.

Bootconfig storage moves among empty, populated and released states. Exit releases data and node areas, clears size and count and brace state, and honors an early release mode. Failed initialization unwinds through the same exit path after setting diagnostics.
Sorted array search entry forwards caller key, base, element count, element width and comparator to a shared inline helper and returns the helper result.

Geometry descriptor carries key length in words plus capacities for pairs and for key words. Three global instances cover narrow, word sized and wide keys with capacities scaled from node size and word width.

Node storage extent is the larger of cache line extent and 128 units. Derived limits include words per 64 bit quantity from word width and a maximum key span twice that value, which bounds predecessor and merge buffers.

Node backing allocation and release use a dedicated slab cache established at module load and torn down at unload. Mempool callbacks wrap cache allocation and release and ignore caller private data. Fresh nodes obtained from the mempool are cleared before use.

Each node packs keys at low offsets and values or child links after the key area. Helpers derive slots from geometry, order keys lexicographically by words, copy or clear word spans, assign keys and values by slot, and decrement multiword keys with borrow.

Tree handles start empty with no root and zero height. One initializer attaches a caller supplied mempool while another creates its own empty mempool and reports creation failure. Destruction releases the root and mempool and detaches the handle.

Lookup descends internal levels by first slot not greater than the sought key then scans the leaf for equality, returning the linked value or null when empty or when the path is missing. Update overwrites the value for an existing key or signals absence. Smallest entry retrieval follows first children downward. Predecessor search decrements the key and retries through saved ancestors, rejecting all zero keys and empty trees.

Position search locates the first slot not greater than the sought key and fill search locates the first empty value from a start index. Descent for mutation widens a rightmost key when the sought key exceeds stored coverage, preserving ordering during later steps.

Insertion increases height when the requested level exceeds current depth, splits full nodes around the midpoint into a fresh sibling linked through the parent, shifts slots to open a gap, then stores the new pair. Null values and duplicate keys are forbidden.

Removal deletes the slot and shifts successors down, then either rebalances below the top, shrinks a single child root, or clears a fully drained tree. Rebalancing merges an underfilled node with a neighbor when combined occupancy fits; otherwise neighbors are left separate. Merging an empty child removes its parent link and frees the node.

Tree merge adopts the victim root when the destination is empty, otherwise repeatedly moves the smallest remaining victim entry into the destination until drained, duplicating keys to survive mutation, and propagates allocation failure while rejecting self merge. Ordered visitation invokes a caller callback for each leaf entry with opaque data and a running index; a destructive variant also frees nodes and resets the handle, with width adapters narrowing keys for callers and a null callback selecting a no operation action.

Bucket lock allocation derives table size from processor count, a per processor multiplier with an upper cap, and a caller maximum, allocates a spin lock array that may use virtual backing, initializes every element with name and class identity, and publishes a mask one less than size. Release frees the array.

Bucket tables require per element spin initialization plus dependency registration before publication. Module bug list changes and traversals use read copy update protection so fault path lookups avoid blocking synchronization.

Fault address resolution scans the built in bug table then module tables, computing effective addresses under either relative or absolute encodings. File and line decoding honors verbosity configuration while format decoding honors architecture support and treats null or empty encodings as absent. Non modular builds always report no module match.

Module setup scans section headers for the bug table section, records its base and entry count, and links the module into the global list; teardown unlinks it. The local logging prefix macro leaves messages unchanged.

Tree paths assume non null values on insertion, unique keys, valid levels, and expected occupancy during shrink and merge; violations trigger fatal checks. Callers must serialize mutation and validate keys because no internal locking or duplicate tolerance is shown.

Bootconfig initialization is single shot until explicit exit; a second attempt fails as busy. Parse or verify failures release all owned memory and expose failure position and diagnostic text through optional outputs.
